```jac
"""studio - multi-tenant identity + per-user artifact paths.

The security model: in a plain `def` (= `def:priv`) endpoint `root` is the caller's
OWN isolated root, so `jid(root)` is the stable per-user identity. Graph-backed data
(chats, messages, eval nodes, workspaces) is therefore isolated for free by the
framework — `[root -->][?:Chat]` only ever returns the caller's chats. See
`jac guide jac-sv-auth` + `jac-sv-multi-user`.

This module namespaces the NON-graph artifacts (training / eval / builder / cpt job
files + logs) under a per-user directory, so one tenant cannot list, read, stop, or
delete another tenant's detached jobs by guessing a name or id. Defense-in-depth on
top of the graph isolation.

INVARIANT: only call `uid()` / `user_*()` from inside a request context (a `def`
endpoint body, or a helper invoked from one). `root` is unbound outside a served
request, so these must never run at import time or in a plain `jac run` script.
"""

import os;
import models;
import paths;
import from pathlib { Path }
import from jaclang { JacRuntime }

"""True when the server was started for local single-user desktop use
(start.sh sets JAC_LOCAL_USER=1). The client uses this to auto-provision a
local session and skip the login screen. `def:pub` so a logged-out client can
read it; prod (start_prod.sh) leaves the env unset, so this returns False and
the real login gate is shown."""
def:pub local_mode() -> bool { ... }

# Fixed credentials for the implicit local desktop user. Only ever used against
# a JAC_LOCAL_USER server on the user's own machine; the graph is local.
glob LOCAL_EMAIL: str = "local@studio.local";
glob LOCAL_PASSWORD: str = "local-desktop-session";

"""Local-desktop auto-session: register (idempotent) + login the implicit local
user IN-PROCESS and return a JWT.

Why this exists: the desktop webview target can't reach `/user/register` +
`/user/login` over HTTP. The only HTTP server in webview mode is the loopback
oauth broker (the `studio` binary), which serves `/__jac/*` + static files and
does NOT proxy `/user/*` to the in-process jac-scale server (that proxying is
wired only in CEF mode via sv_bridge). The in-process API is reachable only
through the native `__jac_invoke` bridge, which dispatches `/walker/*` and
`/function/*` — so the client calls THIS endpoint over that bridge and gets
back a token it can `jacSetToken()` with, after which every authenticated
`def:priv` call succeeds.

Mints the token via `Jac.get_user_manager(base_path=...)` directly — the same
factory `JacAPIServer` itself calls at startup (`Jac.get_user_manager` ->
`UserManager(base_path=...)`), pointed at the same `<base_path>/.jac/data/main.db`
SQLite file the running server's own UserManager reads/writes. Tokens are
opaque `secrets.token_urlsafe` strings looked up by exact match (no JWT, no
secret to reproduce) — a second UserManager instance writing to the same file
is safe and immediately valid.

(An earlier version of this routed through a desktop-webview-only in-process
TestClient bridge; that module does not exist in this jaclang install for
ANY target, desktop included, so it always failed here — hence the rewrite.)

Returns "" on any failure or when not in local mode; the client then falls
back to the production login gate. `def:pub` (no auth) so a logged-out client
can bootstrap. The `local_mode()` guard is defense-in-depth — prod never calls
this."""
def:pub local_session() -> str { ... }

"""Lightweight auth probe for the client keepalive loop. `def:priv` — a 401 means
the JWT expired or is invalid; the client then re-mints (local) or shows login."""
def session_alive() -> bool { ... }

"""Stable per-user id — the caller's root jid. Request-context only."""
def uid() -> str { ... }

"""Per-user results tree: <data_root>/results/users/<uid>/.

Everything a user's SFT/DPO training, eval, and builder jobs write lands here, so
the list/stop/delete endpoints are scoped to the caller. Callers mkdir it on first
use (parents=True, exist_ok=True)."""
def user_results_dir() -> Path { ... }

"""Per-user path under the shared workspace checkout (used by CPT, whose corpus
lives in the repo). <workspace_root>/<rel_prefix>/users/<uid>/<rest>."""
def user_workspace_dir(rel_prefix: str, rest: str = "") -> Path { ... }
```

```jac
"""useConfirmReset — auto-disarms the app's two-click "SURE?" destructive confirms.

The two-click pattern (first click arms the button and flips its label to
"SURE?", second click actually deletes) lives in JmsProjects (project DELETE),
Evals (eval-history DEL) and WorkspaceSettings (workspace DELETE + section ✕).
Armed state used to be sticky: nothing but a second click cleared it, so a
button could sit armed indefinitely and a stray click on the same screen
position minutes later silently deleted a project / eval / workspace. Nothing in
this app is recoverable, so that was a data-loss bug, not a cosmetic one.

This hook is the single disarm mechanism for all of them. Call it once per
confirm state var, UNCONDITIONALLY (it wraps a `useEffect`, so it must sit above
any early `return` in the component), passing:

  * `armed` — the confirm state as a string. "" means nothing is armed. Passing
    the id (not a bool) means re-arming on a DIFFERENT row re-fires the effect
    and restarts that row's timer.
  * `reset` — a nullary callback that clears the confirm var.
  * `ms`    — timeout backstop, default 4s.

Three ways it disarms, all with the same `reset`:

  1. Escape — a document keydown, matching the Escape-closes-a-dialog wiring in
     Shortcuts.cl.jac / WorkspaceSettings.cl.jac. Deliberately does NOT
     stopPropagation: in a drawer, Escape disarming the button and closing the
     drawer are both correct.
  2. Pointer-down anywhere that is not inside the armed button. The armed button
     must carry `data-confirm-armed` (see CONFIRM_ARMED_SEL) for the hit test.
     `mousedown`, not `click`, on purpose: mousedown lands BEFORE React's click
     handler re-renders the row, so the attribute is still in the DOM when the
     second (confirming) click starts and the hit test correctly skips it.
  3. A 4s timeout, re-armed from scratch every time `armed` changes and cleared
     in the effect cleanup — same effect-local-timer-id shape as Toast's
     auto-dismiss, so nothing leaks across re-renders or unmount.
"""

import from react { useEffect }

"""The armed button must render `data-confirm-armed={"1" if armed else None}`
(React drops the attribute for a None value), which is what this selector finds."""
glob:pub CONFIRM_ARMED_SEL: str = "[data-confirm-armed]";

def:pub useConfirmReset(armed: str, reset: any, ms: float = 4000.0) { ... }
```

```jac
module so hit-testing and drawing cannot drift apart. Positions are free-form
px, so an edge can travel any direction; control handles are axis-aligned along
the dominant axis, keeping tangents exact and the arrowhead a fixed triangle."""

import from ...models { StepView }

glob NODE_W: float = 176.0,

     # whether or not a step has a blurb - the geometry is one constant.

     EDGE_ZONE: float = 12.0,
     # Working room kept beyond the furthest step, so there is always
     # somewhere to drag to without the canvas jumping.

# Does this transition travel backwards? One definition, shared by the canvas
# and the inspector, so the two renderings of the same edge cannot disagree.
# Node size is constant, so top-left deltas equal centre deltas.
def isBackEdge(fx: float, fy: float, tx: float, ty: float) -> bool { ... }


# How close to a node's edge counts as grabbing its border (the wire port)
# rather than its body (a move).
# The position a step is actually drawn at: its live drag override, else the
# persisted one.

    steps: list[StepView], live: dict[str, list[float]], px: float, py: float
) -> dict[str, any] { ... }


# The curve between two node rects, leaving and entering through the borders
# that face each other along the dominant axis. `twoWay` shifts it sideways so
# an A→B / B→A pair reads as two arcs. Returns the path, arrowhead, true
# midpoint (for the chip) and `back` (right-to-left or bottom-to-top travel).
def wire(x1: float, y1: float, x2: float, y2: float, twoWay: bool) -> dict[str, any] { ... }
```

```jac
"""studio - BYO GPU clusters (bring-your-own SSH box).

Replaces the Spheron *marketplace* flow (search offers → deploy → destroy via a
vendor REST API) with a vendor-neutral one: the user generates an ed25519
keypair HERE (this app runs on their own machine), pastes the PUBLIC half into
whatever GPU console they like (Spheron dashboard, RunPod, Lambda, a bare-metal
box's authorized_keys), gets an ssh connection string back, and pastes that in.
JMS parses it, probes it, and stores it as a reusable `Cluster` that any
training run can target. No API key, no billing integration, no provider SDK.

Key material policy
  * The PRIVATE key NEVER enters the OSP graph. It is written to
    `~/.jms/ssh_keys/<key_id>` (0600) — outside the git repo on purpose, so
    `paths.studio_root()` (the jms/ dir, which IS inside the repo) is never a
    candidate. Override the directory with `JMS_SSH_KEY_DIR` (tests use this).
  * Only the PUBLIC key + its SHA256 fingerprint live on the graph. Both are
    safe to return to the client and to log — that is the whole point of a
    public key. crypto.sv.jac is therefore NOT used here: there is no secret at
    rest in the graph to encrypt.
  * Audit records carry ids/labels/hosts only — never a key path, never key
    material, never a full ssh command.

Multi-tenancy: `SshKey` and `Cluster` hang off the CALLER's own root
(`[root -->][?:Type]`), same shape as spheron.sv.jac's `SpheronCred` /
`SpheronDeployment`, so one tenant can never see or use another's cluster.

Return convention (matches spheron.sv.jac exactly): every client-facing `def`
returns a dict that always contains `ok: bool` and `error: str`. `ok=True`
means the operation succeeded; a failed *connection probe* is NOT a failed
operation (see `add_cluster`) — that is reported via `test_ok`/`test_message`.

Checker notes (jaclang 0.16.1): `root ++> X(...)` evaluates to a LIST — bind
the node first and connect on its own statement (same trick spheron.sv.jac:495
uses). `re` match groups are untyped, so every group read is wrapped in str().
"""

import re;
import shlex;
import subprocess;
import datetime;
import audit;
import jobs;
import from pathlib { Path }
import from uuid { uuid4 }

# Marker echoed by the remote end of a successful probe.
glob PROBE_MARKER: str = "JMS_PROBE_OK";

glob PROBE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S: int = 8;
glob PROBE_TIMEOUT_S: int = 15;
glob KEYGEN_TIMEOUT_S: int = 15;

"""One locally generated ed25519 keypair owned by the caller.
```
